relocation.title: Decide and plan
items: Write down why you are moving and the date you would like to be settled by
Talk to a lender about what you can afford, and get pre-approved before you shop
If your employer is paying for any of the move, ask what is covered and what the tax treatment is
Ask a tax professional how a move to Tennessee affects your situation, especially if you will keep working for an employer in another state
Compare areas by the numbers: price, property tax, commute and distance to what matters to you
Pick two or three areas to visit, and plan a trip to see them
relocation.tip: Tip: your pre-approval letter is what makes an offer from out of state credible, so get it early.

relocation.title: Choose where to live
items: Visit the areas you picked, and drive the real commute at the time of day you would drive it
For any home you are serious about, check school assignment with the school district using the exact address
Look up the property tax on the exact address with the county, not just the listing's figure
Ask about HOA dues, rules and fees for any community you like
Tour homes in person or by live video, and ask about utility costs, age of the roof, HVAC and water heater

relocation.title: Buy, and sell where you live now
items: Make an offer and agree on the closing date that fits your move
If you own a home now, talk to an agent licensed in that state about when to list and how to line up both closings
Schedule your home inspection, and consider a sewer scope, radon and termite inspections
Arrange homeowner's insurance and send proof of coverage to your lender
Keep your job, credit and bank accounts steady until you close, and answer your lender quickly

relocation.title: Book the move
items: Get quotes from at least three licensed moving companies, and check each one's registration
Schedule utilities to start on move-in day: electric, water, gas, trash and internet
Set up mail forwarding and tell your bank, card companies and employer your new address
Request medical, dental, vet and school records from your current providers
Decide what to sell, donate or leave behind before the movers arrive

relocation.title: Move week
items: Do your final walkthrough of the new home before closing
Confirm the closing time, how you will get the keys and what to bring
Photograph meter readings and any existing damage on move-in day
Keep your important papers, medications and valuables with you, not on the truck

relocation.title: Your first 30 days in Tennessee
items: Get a Tennessee driver license within 30 days of establishing residency, at a full-service Driver Services Center
Register your vehicle through your county clerk, and bring your out-of-state registration
Register to vote and update your address with the IRS, your employer and your insurers
Check whether you qualify for any property tax relief or exemptions, and note the county's appeal dates
Introduce yourself to your neighbors, and save the contact details for your city and county services
relocation.tip: Tip: the license and vehicle rules change, so confirm each one on the state's website before you go.
